title: Air India Express Adds 135 Daily Gulf Departures in Its Biggest-Ever Winter Schedule
excerpt: The Tata Group carrier's Winter 2026 network links 23 Indian cities with 12 West Asia gateways through 88 non-stop routes — a bounce-back from February's airspace crisis that goes well beyond pre-crisis levels.
body:
• Air India Express will operate up to 135 daily departures to West Asia this winter across 88 non-stop city pairs, connecting 23 Indian cities with 12 gateways in Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE.
  • The Winter 2026 schedule, effective October 25 and running through March 27, 2027, is the airline's largest ever: about 585 daily flights, with weekly operations up roughly 30% over summer.
  • New Gulf links include Delhi–Riyadh, Lucknow–Riyadh, Kochi–Kuwait, Mumbai–Kuwait, Amritsar–Abu Dhabi, Chandigarh–Sharjah, plus new Dubai and Abu Dhabi services to Goa.
  • Winter is peak Gulf–India travel season, spanning Diwali and the year-end holidays. The new tier-2 frequencies cut the need to route through Delhi or Mumbai; bookings are open on airindiaexpress.com and the app, with retrofitted aircraft on several West Asia routes.

Air India Express on Monday announced an expanded India–West Asia network under its Winter 2026 schedule, its largest winter programme ever. The airline will operate up to 135 daily departures to West Asia across 88 non-stop city-pair routes, linking 23 Indian cities with 12 gateways in Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE. The Gulf remains the biggest component of its international network, which will run up to 150 daily international departures to 99 destinations worldwide this winter.

Context and background

The scale of the plan looks different against what the airline flew this year. Air India Express took off in 2005 as the low-cost arm of Air India, built around a single market: the Gulf, carrying the expatriate workforce from southern India. The Tata Group's January 2022 takeover turned it into the group's value carrier, folding in AirAsia India with the merger done in October 2024.

"At 150 international departures a day, it sits 11% above the airline's 2025 peak and 23% above August."

Through 2025 the merged airline averaged roughly 330 to 380 domestic and 110 to 135 international departures a day, according to DGCA data analysed by aviation publication Network Thoughts. Then came the West Asia crisis: when regional airspace closed at the end of February 2026, the airline suspended scheduled flights to the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar and Bahrain, running ad-hoc relief flights instead. International departures collapsed from 114 a day in February to 41 in March, climbing back only to 122 by August.

Set against those numbers, the winter plan is a step beyond recovery. At 150 international departures a day, it sits 11% above the airline's 2025 peak and 23% above August. Weekly operations climb from about 3,150 flights this summer to nearly 4,100 this winter — a jump of roughly 30% in a single season.

Impact and analysis

The new international routes follow the old Air India Express playbook, extended north and west. Lucknow, Bhopal, Chandigarh, Amritsar, Surat and Mangaluru gain Gulf links, and Saudi Arabia gets three new Riyadh routes from Delhi, Lucknow and Thiruvananthapuram. Ras Al Khaimah services from Lucknow and Mangaluru show the airline using secondary Emirates airports to reach catchments the bigger hubs miss. Core hubs — Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Kochi, Kozhikode and Hyderabad — also get frequency increases on the busiest corridors: Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Dammam, Jeddah, Riyadh, Doha, Muscat, Kuwait City and Al Ain.

Only 36 of the more than 40 new routes have been named so far, adding about 176 weekly flights against overall growth of roughly 950 — most of the expansion is extra frequencies on existing routes. The tier-2 Gulf strategy remains the carrier's natural strength: foreign carriers are limited to designated points of call in India, leaving cities like Lucknow, Bhopal, Surat and Mangaluru largely to Indian airlines, where the rival is IndiGo. The quieter shift is network scale: weekly one-stop connections jump from about 1,330 to nearly 1,600, with Bengaluru, Delhi and the southern gateways acting as connecting points. Air India Express is slowly becoming a network airline, not just a point-to-point Gulf carrier.

Diaspora angle

West Asia hosts one of the largest overseas Indian communities in the world, and the airline framed the expansion around its core passengers: people travelling for work, family and leisure. Winter is the peak window — Diwali, the year-end holidays, and school breaks drive the busiest visiting-friends-and-relatives traffic of the year. For Gulf-based NRIs from tier-2 cities, a direct Lucknow–Riyadh or Mangaluru–Kuwait flight replaces a tiring one-stop trip through Delhi or Mumbai. More frequencies on core corridors also mean more choice and, over time, more fare pressure.

What's next

The schedule rolls out in phases from October 25, 2026, and runs through March 27, 2027, alongside new domestic routes and retrofitted aircraft. The real test is whether this capacity survives into summer 2027, when leisure demand softens and yields come under pressure. At 585 daily departures on 105-plus aircraft, each jet averages over five and a half sectors a day — a pace that leaves little room for disruption. Gulf travellers should book early for the December–January peak.
